newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Hi-Bred sees good seed corn supply.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Hi-Bred sees good seed corn supply.

text.p: Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc said Monday it expects a good supply of high quality seed corn in 1997.

"Corn acreage in North America and around the world is expected to stay high as farmers respond to continued strong worldwide demand for feed grains," Charles Johnson, president, said in a statement. "Our seed corn harvest is moving along well and should give us a good supply of high quality seed for 1997."

He added that while the 1996 harvest is just underway in the Midwest, Pioneer is encouraged with the performance of its corn hybrids, soybeans and other products in early comparisons with the competition.
Earlier, Pioneer reported a loss for the fourth quarter of $0.42 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.59. For all of fiscal 1996, it earned $2.68, up from $2.16 last year.
Pioneer said its return on ending equity (ROE) was 22 percent in fiscal 1996. The company first reached its goal of 20 percent in fiscal 1994 and sustained it since then.
Pioneer said North American hybrid seed corn volume in 1996 was 11 percent higher than a year ago and soybean volume was three percent higher.
